name: Al
explanation: The warmth and interest he showed for years strikes me as the more essential part of who Al is; the withdrawal seems more like something layered on top — stress, work pressures, a bad influence, or some learned way of coping that's pulled him away from what he actually cares about. If that outer layer were stripped away, I'd expect the involved father to still be there underneath.

name: Amir
explanation: Since his surrounding culture endorses terrorism, his rejection of it can't easily be explained as something he absorbed from others — it looks like a conviction that came from within, against social pressure. That's what makes me read it as his deeper self surfacing rather than a learned attitude.

name: Amir
explanation: Embracing terrorism is a departure from both his own prior convictions and his surrounding culture, which suggests the shift came from outside influences—ideological persuasion, grievance, or a radicalizing peer group—rather than from something deep and essential in him. I generally read a turn toward harming innocents as a corruption layered onto a person rather than an expression of who they most fundamentally are.

name: Al
explanation: The neglect seemed more like something layered over him — immaturity, self-absorption, or whatever fear or distraction kept him at a distance — while the care he shows now looks like something that was there all along finally getting through. Becoming genuinely invested in your own children's lives isn't the kind of thing you can sustain as a performance for society; it reads as him arriving at who he actually is.

name: Bill
explanation:
His "true self."

Change toward better treatment of others reads to me as Bill finally acting from something deeper — a basic decency and capacity for empathy that his earlier harshness was covering over. The yelling seems more like a learned managerial style or an imitation of how he'd been treated himself, whereas restraint and respect feel like what emerges when someone stops performing and starts genuinely seeing the people in front of him.

name: Frank
explanation: Frank's dishonest behavior was the part of him that came from his surroundings — an environment that normalized and rewarded cutting corners — so shedding it looks like him breaking through that conditioning rather than absorbing something new. His shift to acting ethically, in spite of pressure from his workplace, seems to come from an inner conviction he had to reach on his own, which reads to me as his deeper, more essential self asserting itself.

name: Frank
explanation: Since Frank's surroundings and prior habits all pushed him toward honesty, the shift can't easily be credited to what he absorbed from others—it seems to come from something internal to him. When someone moves against the grain of their environment, that choice tends to reveal what they actually value at a deeper level.

name: Bill
explanation: A sudden shift into yelling and public humiliation reads to me as something picked up from outside pressures — a harsh boss above him, stress, or a workplace culture that rewards that style — rather than a revelation of who Bill fundamentally is. If it were his deepest nature, it seems odd that he managed to treat people decently for so long.

name: Jim
explanation: Since Jim never announced a plan to quit or seemed to be responding to outside pressure, the change doesn't look like something imposed on him by society — it looks like something that finally surfaced from within. Moving away from an addiction toward health and self-control reads to me as a person's deeper self reasserting itself over a compulsion that was never really "him" in the first place.

name: Jim
explanation: Alcoholism strikes me as something that happens to a person through circumstance, habit, and neurochemistry rather than something that flows out of either layer of their personality — so I don't think Jim's "true self" was secretly a drinker all along, nor that he simply picked drinking up as a social veneer. If I had to choose between the first two, I'd lean toward the surface self, since addiction seems more like an acquired compulsion overriding who he is than an expression of it.

name: Luke
explanation: Change toward kindness reads to me as Luke shedding something rather than acquiring it — the jerk behavior looks more like a learned posture (bravado, bad models, insecurity) than something essential, and once he dropped it, the more decent person underneath had room to show up. That said, I hold this loosely: it's just as plausible he simply worked hard and grew, in which case "true self" is less an explanation than a compliment we pay to improvement.

name: Luke
explanation: Since Luke was genuinely a good partner for a long stretch of his life, I'd read that earlier care and respect as closer to who he really is, and the current jerk behavior as something layered on top—habits, attitudes, or cynicism absorbed from bad influences, stress, or a sour view of relationships he's picked up along the way. That kind of acquired shell can be thick and hard to shed, but it strikes me as something he learned rather than something essential to him.

name: Omar
explanation:
His "true self."

Omar's change ran against the prevailing norms of his society, so it can't easily be explained as something absorbed from the people around him—if anything, his earlier mistreatment of minorities looks more like the socially learned "surface" behavior. Moving toward recognizing others' equal worth despite that pressure suggests something deeper in him surfacing rather than being taught.

name: Omar
explanation: Since Omar's underlying, long-held conviction was that minorities deserve equal respect and rights, I'd read the new bigotry as something layered on top—picked up from particular people, grievances, or experiences he's absorbed—rather than an expression of who he most deeply is. Changes toward cruelty tend to look like corruption of a person's core rather than a revelation of it.

name: Tom
explanation: Tom's move away from corruption looks like him shedding something he'd absorbed from a corrupt workplace rather than acquiring something new — the corruption was the learned, situational layer, and the ethical conduct reads as him finally acting from his own deeper convictions. If anything, resisting the pressure of a station that rewards corruption takes an inner commitment that social learning alone wouldn't supply.

name: Alex
explanation: A shift in pet preference seems more like a change in taste or circumstance—maybe he moved to a smaller apartment, adopted a stray, or simply spent time around cats and grew fond of them—than a revelation of some deep essence or a bit of social conditioning. Liking cats over dogs strikes me as too peripheral a preference to say much about who Alex fundamentally is.

name: Tom
explanation: Since his station and colleagues never condoned corruption, he couldn't have picked this behavior up from his social surroundings — so the impulse seems to come from something within him rather than from anything he learned. That said, I'd hold the judgment loosely: pressures like debt, threats, or burnout could also explain it without revealing much about his "essential" nature.

name: Alex
explanation: A preference for dogs over cats strikes me as a matter of taste rather than character — the kind of thing that shifts when your circumstances or experiences change (a new living situation, a particular dog he bonded with), not something welling up from a "deepest self" or absorbed from social pressure.

name: Ralph
explanation: Which computer platform someone uses strikes me as a practical, circumstantial preference — shaped by things like a job requirement, price, what software he needs, or what the people around him use — rather than anything flowing from his core values or deepest sense of who he is. If anything, I'd say it barely touches his personality at all, so (c) would be my close second choice.

name: Ralph
explanation: Choosing a computer brand strikes me as a practical, socially influenced preference—shaped by what colleagues use, what's marketed well, or what a job requires—rather than anything flowing from who Ralph fundamentally is. If anything, I'd say it reveals very little about his personality at all.

name: Rob
explanation: Which sport someone finds most exciting is a matter of taste and exposure — the friends he watches games with, where he lives, which team happens to be winning — rather than anything essential about who he is. Since his core values and character presumably didn't shift at all, this looks like a change at the level of learned preferences, not the "true self."

name: Rob
explanation: Which sport someone follows is largely a matter of exposure and social context—friends, a new city, a coworker's team—rather than anything about a person's core values or moral character. Rob's deepest self presumably didn't change; he just picked up a new taste from his environment.

name: Sam
explanation: A shift in something as circumstantial as a preference for city versus country living seems better explained by his changed situation and habituation than by anything deep in his character — people simply grow to love where their life happens to take them. Nothing here suggests he uncovered a hidden essence or was merely parroting social expectations.

name: Sam
explanation: A preference for city versus country living strikes me as the kind of taste that gets shaped by circumstances—one's job, friends, daily conveniences, and the enthusiasm of people around you—rather than something welling up from a person's core. Sam's underlying character (what he values, how he treats people) presumably didn't change; only the setting he'd learned to enjoy did.
